response.passage: Consumer protection is essential for everyone, regardless of their education or economic status, because exploitation can happen to any buyer in any marketplace. Sellers may use unfair practices like adulteration or overcharging, even in high-end branded stores, so consumers must remain vigilant everywhere. To help buyers identify quality, the government mandates certification marks. For instance, the ISI mark is used for industrial and electrical goods, while the Agmark is specifically for agricultural products. These symbols act as a guarantee of quality and safety standards. If a consumer feels cheated, they do not need to approach the highest court in the land for every issue. Instead, the Consumer Protection Act (COPRA) established a three-tier quasi-judicial machinery. Consumers can file complaints at the District, State, or National level depending on the value of the goods or services and the compensation claimed. This system ensures that justice is accessible and affordable for all citizens, moving away from the idea that only the wealthy can seek legal redressal. By understanding these rights and the proper channels for grievances, every shopper can protect themselves from unfair trade practices effectively.
response.summary: Consumer protection is a universal right that applies to all buyers regardless of their background. The government provides certification marks and a tiered court system to ensure quality and fair redressal for everyone.
